chapters.1.summary: In the beginning God creates the heavens and the earth. He speaks, and light, sky, land, and plants appear over three days. Sun, moon, stars, sea animals, and birds follow. On the sixth day he makes land animals and then people. He makes people in his own image, male and female. He blesses them and tells them to fill the earth and rule the animals. He gives plants as food to people and animals. God sees all he has made and calls it very good.
chapters.1.lds: Moses 2 places human creation within God’s work. Verse 27 says God made male and female in his image. How should that shape the way you treat people?
chapters.2.summary: God finishes his work, rests on the seventh day, and makes that day holy. Then the LORD God forms a man from dust and breathes life into him. God plants a garden in Eden with a river and two named trees. He puts the man there to work it and keep it. He forbids one tree and warns of death. God says it is not good for the man to be alone. The man names the animals, but none is a helper like him. God makes a woman from his rib, and the man welcomes her as his flesh.
chapters.2.lds: Moses 3 connects the garden with God’s commands. The man has work and food but is alone (verse 18). What need does the woman answer in verse 23?
chapters.3.summary: The serpent asks the woman what God really said. She repeats the command, and the serpent says she will not die. She sees the fruit is good, eats, and gives some to her husband. Their eyes open, and they cover themselves and hide. God asks where the man is and whether he ate. The man blames the woman, and the woman blames the serpent. God curses the serpent and the ground, and speaks of pain and hard work. He clothes them with skins and sends them out of Eden.
chapters.3.lds: Moses 4 expands the garden account. Second Nephi 2 connects the Fall with choice and redemption. The man answers God by blaming two others (verse 12). Whom does he blame?
chapters.4.summary: Eve bears Cain and then Abel. Cain farms, and Abel keeps sheep. Both bring offerings, and the LORD accepts Abel’s but not Cain’s. The LORD warns Cain that sin crouches at the door. Cain kills Abel in the field and asks if he is his brother’s keeper. The LORD sends Cain away as a wanderer but marks him for protection. Cain’s family builds a city, and Lamech boasts of killing a man. Eve bears Seth, and people begin to call on the LORD’s name.
chapters.4.lds: Moses 5 adds gospel teaching after the Fall. The LORD warns Cain before he kills (verse 7). What does the warning say Cain can still do?
chapters.5.summary: This is the family record from Adam to Noah. God made people in his likeness, and Adam fathers Seth in his own likeness. Each entry gives a father’s age, his son, his total years, and his death. The years are very long, up to 969 for Methuselah. Enoch’s entry is different. He walks with God, and God takes him. Lamech names his son Noah and hopes for comfort from the cursed ground. Noah fathers Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
chapters.5.lds: Moses 6–7 expands Enoch’s account. Every entry but one ends with “then he died.” What does verse 24 say about Enoch?
chapters.6.summary: People multiply, and God’s sons take human daughters as wives. The LORD says man’s days will be 120 years. He sees that human thoughts are evil all the time, and he is grieved. He decides to wipe out people and animals. But Noah finds favor and walks with God. God tells Noah the earth is filled with violence. He orders a ship of gopher wood with three levels and one door. Noah is to bring his family, pairs of animals, and food, and he obeys.
chapters.6.lds: Moses 8 describes Noah’s preaching before the flood. Verse 9 says Noah “walked with God.” What does verse 22 say he did with God’s orders?
chapters.7.summary: The LORD tells Noah to enter the ship with his household. Noah takes seven pairs of clean animals and one pair of the others. Noah is six hundred years old. After seven days the deep bursts open and the sky’s windows open. Rain falls forty days and nights. Noah’s family and the animals go in, and the LORD shuts him in. The water lifts the ship and covers the high mountains. Everything on dry land dies, and only those in the ship remain.
chapters.7.lds: The Church manual reads Noah’s deliverance within God’s dealings with humanity. Verse 5 says Noah did all the LORD commanded. What does the LORD do for Noah in verse 16?
chapters.8.summary: God remembers Noah and the animals and sends a wind. The water goes down, and the ship rests on the mountains of Ararat. Noah sends out a raven and then a dove. The dove comes back with an olive leaf, then does not return. God tells Noah to leave the ship with his family and the animals. Noah builds an altar and offers burnt offerings. The LORD says he will not again curse the ground or strike every living thing. Seedtime and harvest, summer and winter, day and night will not stop.
chapters.8.lds: Noah worships after deliverance. Verse 1 says God “remembered Noah.” What does God promise about seasons in verse 22?
chapters.9.summary: God blesses Noah and his sons and tells them to fill the earth. Animals will fear them, and they may eat meat but not blood. God will demand a reckoning for human life, because he made people in his image. He makes a covenant with Noah, his family, and every living creature. No flood will destroy the earth again, and the rainbow is the sign. Noah plants a vineyard and gets drunk. Ham sees his father naked, and Shem and Japheth cover him. Noah curses Canaan and blesses Shem and Japheth.
chapters.9.lds: A covenant is a sacred agreement. Verse 6 gives a reason not to shed human blood. What is the reason?
chapters.10.summary: This is the family record of Noah’s sons after the flood. Japheth’s line spreads to the coasts and islands. Ham’s line includes Cush, Mizraim, and Canaan. Cush’s son Nimrod is a mighty hunter, and his kingdom begins at Babel. Canaan’s families spread from Sidon toward Gaza. Shem’s line includes Eber, Peleg, and Joktan. Each list ends with families, languages, lands, and nations. From these families the nations spread over the earth.
chapters.10.lds: The family record joins many peoples to common ancestors. Verse 32 says the nations came from one family. How should that shape the way one nation sees another?
chapters.11.summary: All people speak one language and settle on a plain in Shinar. They bake bricks and plan a city with a tower to the sky. They want a name for themselves and fear being scattered. The LORD comes down to see, confuses their language, and scatters them. The city is called Babel. Then the record runs from Shem to Terah. Terah fathers Abram, Nahor, and Haran, and Abram’s wife Sarai has no child. Terah leaves Ur for Canaan but settles in Haran and dies there.
chapters.11.lds: The Church manual contrasts Babel with the covenant family story. The builders want “a name for ourselves” (verse 4). Who promises a great name in 12:2?
chapters.12.summary: The LORD tells Abram to leave his country and his father’s house. He promises a great nation and a blessing for all families through Abram. Abram goes at age seventy-five with Sarai and Lot. In Canaan the LORD promises the land to his offspring, and Abram builds altars. A famine sends him to Egypt. He asks Sarai to say she is his sister, because he fears being killed. Pharaoh takes her and pays Abram well, and the LORD sends plagues. Pharaoh rebukes Abram and sends them away.
chapters.12.lds: Abraham 2 links the covenant with blessing all families. Verse 3 promises blessing to “all the families of the earth.” What happens to Pharaoh’s house when Abram hides the truth (verse 17)?
chapters.13.summary: Abram returns from Egypt to Bethel, rich in livestock, silver, and gold. Lot also has flocks, and the land cannot hold both. Their herdsmen quarrel. Abram asks for no strife and offers Lot his choice of land. Lot sees the well-watered Jordan plain and chooses it. He camps near Sodom, whose men are very wicked. The LORD tells Abram to look all around, for the land will be his. Abram moves to the oaks of Mamre at Hebron and builds an altar.
chapters.13.lds: Abraham gives Lot the first choice. What reason does Abram give for ending the quarrel in verse 8?
chapters.14.summary: Four kings make war on five kings near the Salt Sea. The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah flee, and the winners take goods, food, and people. They take Lot, who lives in Sodom. Abram leads 318 trained men, attacks by night, and brings everyone back. Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, brings bread and wine. He blesses Abram, and Abram gives him a tenth. The king of Sodom offers Abram the goods. Abram refuses even a thread, so the king cannot say he made Abram rich.
chapters.14.lds: Alma 13 expands Melchizedek’s role as a priest. Keep that teaching distinct from Genesis’s brief account. Abram gives to one king and refuses another (verses 20–23). What reason does he give?
chapters.15.summary: The LORD comes to Abram in a vision and says not to fear. Abram says he has no child, and a servant will be his heir. The LORD says his own son will be his heir and shows him the stars. Abram believes, and the LORD counts it as righteousness. Abram asks how he will know the land is his. He cuts animals in half, and a deep sleep and darkness fall on him. The LORD says his offspring will serve in a foreign land four hundred years. A furnace and a torch pass between the pieces, and the LORD makes a covenant.
chapters.15.lds: God’s promise meets Abraham’s fear about an heir. Abram asks how he will know (verse 8). What hard news comes with the answer in verse 13?
chapters.16.summary: Sarai has no children and gives her Egyptian servant Hagar to Abram as a wife. Hagar conceives and looks down on Sarai. Sarai blames Abram, and he says Hagar is in her hand. Sarai treats her harshly, and Hagar runs away. The LORD’s angel finds her by a spring and tells her to return. He promises her many offspring and a son named Ishmael, because the LORD heard. Hagar names the LORD “a God who sees.” She bears Ishmael when Abram is eighty-six.
chapters.16.lds: God sees Hagar in distress. The angel sends her back but also makes a promise (verses 9–11). What does the name Ishmael say the LORD has done?
chapters.17.summary: Abram is ninety-nine when the LORD appears as God Almighty. God makes a covenant: many nations will come from Abram, and Canaan will be theirs. God changes his name to Abraham. Every male in his house, even bought servants, must be circumcised as the sign. Sarai’s name becomes Sarah, and she will bear a son. Abraham laughs and asks that Ishmael might live before God. God says Sarah will bear Isaac, and Ishmael will also become a great nation. Abraham circumcises every male in his house that same day.
chapters.17.lds: Abraham 2 links covenant blessings with the gospel. Abraham obeys “in the same day” (verse 23). Who in his house receives the sign?
chapters.18.summary: The LORD appears to Abraham at Mamre as three men stand near his tent. Abraham runs to meet them and serves bread, a calf, butter, and milk. One says Sarah will have a son next year. Sarah laughs to herself, and the LORD asks if anything is too hard for him. The men look toward Sodom. The LORD tells Abraham that the outcry against Sodom is great. Abraham asks if God will kill the righteous with the wicked. He bargains from fifty down, and the LORD will spare the city for ten.
chapters.18.lds: Abraham pleads for other people’s lives. He says the Judge of all the earth should do right (verse 25). For whom is he asking?
chapters.19.summary: Two angels come to Sodom, and Lot urges them to stay in his house. The men of the city surround it and demand the guests. Lot offers his two daughters, and the crowd turns on him. The angels pull Lot in and strike the men blind. They warn that the LORD will destroy the city, but Lot’s sons-in-law think he jokes. At dawn the angels drag Lot, his wife, and his daughters out. Fire and sulfur fall, and Lot’s wife looks back and becomes a pillar of salt. In a cave, Lot’s daughters make him drunk and bear Moab and Ben Ammi.
chapters.19.lds: Lot lingers even after the warning (verse 16). What does the verse say made the angels take his hand?
chapters.20.summary: Abraham moves to Gerar and again says Sarah is his sister. King Abimelech takes her. God warns Abimelech in a dream that she is a man’s wife. Abimelech says he acted with a clean heart, and God agrees. In the morning he asks Abraham why he did this. Abraham says he thought no one there feared God. He adds that Sarah is his half sister. Abimelech gives animals, servants, and silver, and Abraham prays for his house.
chapters.20.lds: Abraham’s fear puts Sarah at risk. He assumed no one in Gerar feared God (verse 11). What do verses 4–8 show about Abimelech?
chapters.21.summary: The LORD does as he said, and Sarah bears Isaac when Abraham is one hundred. Sarah says God has made her laugh. At Isaac’s weaning feast, Sarah sees Hagar’s son mocking. She tells Abraham to send Hagar and the boy away. Abraham is grieved, but God says to listen and promises a nation from the boy. In the wilderness the water runs out, and Hagar weeps. God hears the boy, and Hagar sees a well. Abraham and Abimelech then swear an oath over a well at Beersheba.
chapters.21.lds: God hears Hagar and Ishmael. Verse 17 says God heard the boy “where he is.” What does Hagar see in verse 19?
chapters.22.summary: God tests Abraham and tells him to offer his son Isaac in Moriah. Abraham rises early and travels three days with Isaac and two servants. Isaac carries the wood and asks where the lamb is. Abraham says God will provide the lamb. He builds the altar, binds Isaac, and takes the knife. The LORD’s angel stops him and says he now knows Abraham fears God. Abraham offers a ram caught in a thicket. The LORD swears to bless him and all nations through his offspring.
chapters.22.lds: Jacob 4:5 links Abraham’s offering with the Father’s gift of Christ. Genesis itself stops Isaac’s sacrifice. Isaac asks where the lamb is (verse 7). How does his father answer in verse 8?
chapters.23.summary: Sarah dies at Hebron at age 127, and Abraham mourns her. He tells the Hittites he is a foreigner and asks for a burial place. They offer him the best of their tombs. Abraham asks to buy the cave of Machpelah from Ephron at full price. Ephron offers the field as a gift, then names its worth: four hundred shekels. Abraham weighs out the silver before the people at the city gate. The field, cave, and trees are deeded to him. He buries Sarah there.
chapters.23.lds: Abraham secures a burial place for Sarah. He calls himself “a stranger and a foreigner” (verse 4). Why does he insist on paying in verse 13?
chapters.24.summary: Old Abraham makes his servant swear to find Isaac a wife among his relatives. The servant takes ten camels to the city of Nahor. At the well he prays for a woman who also waters his camels. Rebekah comes and does just that. He gives her gold and learns she is Bethuel’s daughter, of Abraham’s family. He tells her brother Laban the whole story, and the family agrees. They ask Rebekah, and she says, “I will go.” Isaac meets her, marries her, and loves her.
chapters.24.lds: Rebekah agrees to the journey. Her family asks if she will go with the servant (verse 58). What had Abraham said about an unwilling woman in verse 8?
chapters.25.summary: Abraham marries Keturah and has more sons, but he gives all he has to Isaac. He dies at 175, and Isaac and Ishmael bury him beside Sarah. Ishmael’s twelve sons are listed. Isaac prays for Rebekah, who has no child, and she conceives twins. The LORD tells her the elder will serve the younger. Esau is born first, red and hairy, and Jacob follows holding his heel. Esau comes in from the field starving and asks for Jacob’s stew. Jacob asks for the birthright, and Esau swears it away.
chapters.25.lds: The birthright concerns a lasting family responsibility. Esau asks what good the birthright is to him (verse 32). What does verse 34 say about his choice?
chapters.26.summary: In a famine the LORD tells Isaac to stay and not go to Egypt. He repeats to Isaac the oath he swore to Abraham. In Gerar Isaac says Rebekah is his sister, and Abimelech finds out and rebukes him. Isaac’s crops yield a hundredfold, and the Philistines envy him. They fill his father’s wells with earth and send him away. Isaac’s men dig wells, and the herdsmen of Gerar claim two of them. He moves again, digs a third, and names it Rehoboth for the room they found. Abimelech then comes to make a peace oath at Beersheba.
chapters.26.lds: God renews the promise to Isaac. Isaac gives up two wells without a fight (verses 20–21). What does he say at the third well in verse 22?
chapters.27.summary: Isaac is old and blind and sends Esau to hunt game before he blesses him. Rebekah hears and tells Jacob to bring two goats. She dresses Jacob in Esau’s clothes and covers his hands with goat skins. Jacob tells his father he is Esau. Isaac doubts the voice, feels the hands, and blesses him as lord over his brothers. Esau returns, and Isaac trembles. Esau weeps and begs for a blessing, and plans to kill Jacob. Rebekah tells Jacob to flee to her brother Laban in Haran.
chapters.27.lds: Esau asks his father for a blessing too (verse 38). What does Isaac say he has already given away in verse 37?
chapters.28.summary: Isaac blesses Jacob and sends him to Paddan Aram to marry a daughter of Laban. Esau sees this and marries a daughter of Ishmael. On the way Jacob sleeps with a stone under his head. He dreams of a stairway to heaven with angels going up and down. The LORD promises him the land, many offspring, and his presence everywhere. Jacob wakes and says the LORD is in this place. He sets up the stone, pours oil on it, and names the place Bethel. He vows a tenth to God if God brings him home in peace.
chapters.28.lds: God meets Jacob while he travels away from home. Jacob says, “The LORD is in this place, and I didn’t know it” (verse 16). What had the LORD just promised in verse 15?
chapters.29.summary: Jacob reaches a well near Haran and meets Rachel, Laban’s daughter. He rolls the stone away, waters her sheep, and weeps. Laban welcomes him as family. Jacob loves Rachel and works seven years for her. At the wedding feast Laban brings him Leah in the evening. Jacob protests, and Laban says the younger is not given before the firstborn. Jacob marries Rachel a week later and works seven more years. The LORD sees that Leah is unloved, and she bears Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah.
chapters.29.lds: God sees Leah’s pain. Jacob asks Laban why he deceived him (verse 25). Whom had Jacob deceived in chapter 27?
chapters.30.summary: Rachel has no children and envies Leah. She gives her servant Bilhah to Jacob, and Bilhah bears Dan and Naphtali. Leah gives her servant Zilpah, who bears Gad and Asher. Rachel trades a night with Jacob for Leah’s mandrake plants. Leah bears Issachar, Zebulun, and a daughter, Dinah. God remembers Rachel, and she bears Joseph. Jacob asks to go home, and Laban asks him to stay for wages. Jacob takes the spotted and dark animals as pay, and his flocks grow large.
chapters.30.lds: The children’s names reveal hope and distress. Leah says Rachel has “taken away my husband” (verse 15). What do the two sisters trade?
chapters.31.summary: Laban’s sons say Jacob took their father’s wealth, and Laban’s face turns cold. The LORD tells Jacob to return home. Jacob tells Rachel and Leah that Laban changed his wages ten times. They agree to go, saying their father sold them. Jacob leaves in secret, and Rachel steals her father’s household idols. Laban chases them, but God warns him in a dream. He searches the tents and finds nothing, and Jacob lists twenty years of hard service. The two men pile stones as a border and swear to do no harm.
chapters.31.lds: Jacob and Laban set a boundary. Rachel and Leah say their father “has sold us” (verse 15). What do they tell Jacob to do in verse 16?
chapters.32.summary: Angels meet Jacob on his way. He sends word to Esau, and hears that Esau is coming with four hundred men. Jacob is afraid and splits his camp in two. He prays, saying he is not worthy, and asks God to save him from Esau. He sends herds ahead as a gift, with space between them. That night he sends his family across the Jabbok and is left alone. A man wrestles with him until dawn and strains his hip. The man names him Israel, and Jacob limps away from Peniel.
chapters.32.lds: Jacob receives the name Israel after a struggle. Jacob tells God, “I fear him” (verse 11). What promise does he remind God of in verse 12?
chapters.33.summary: Jacob sees Esau coming with four hundred men. He lines up the women and children and goes ahead, bowing seven times. Esau runs to him, hugs him, and they weep. Esau asks about the family and about the herds he met. Esau says he has enough, but Jacob urges him to take the gift. Esau offers to travel together, but Jacob says his children and flocks are slow. Esau returns to Seir. Jacob goes to Succoth and then Shechem, buys land, and builds an altar.
chapters.33.lds: Esau welcomes Jacob. Jacob says seeing Esau’s face is like seeing “the face of God” (verse 10). What did Esau do in verse 4?
chapters.34.summary: Dinah, Leah’s daughter, goes out to visit the women of the land. Shechem, the prince’s son, takes her, lies with her, and shames her. He then wants to marry her, and his father Hamor asks Jacob. Jacob’s sons answer with deceit: every male in the city must be circumcised. On the third day Simeon and Levi kill all the males and take Dinah back. The brothers plunder the city and take the women and children. Jacob says they have put the family in danger. They ask if their sister should be treated like a prostitute.
chapters.34.lds: Dinah suffers violence and her brothers take revenge. The chapter ends with a question (verse 31). Who in the chapter never gets to speak?
chapters.35.summary: God tells Jacob to go up to Bethel and build an altar. Jacob tells his household to put away foreign gods and make themselves clean. They hand over the gods and earrings, and he buries them under an oak. At Bethel God blesses him, repeats the name Israel, and promises the land. Rebekah’s nurse Deborah dies there. On the road Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin and is buried near Bethlehem. Reuben lies with Bilhah, his father’s concubine. Jacob reaches Isaac at Hebron, and Esau and Jacob bury their father.
chapters.35.lds: Jacob returns to worship amid family loss. Before going to Bethel, Jacob gives three orders (verse 2). What must the household put away?
chapters.36.summary: This is the family record of Esau, who is also called Edom. Esau’s wives bear him five sons in Canaan. He moves to Seir, because the land cannot hold both brothers’ herds. His sons and grandsons become chiefs of Edom. The Horites, who lived in Seir, are listed with their chiefs. Eight kings rule Edom before Israel has any king. No king in the list is the son of the king before him. The list ends with Esau as the father of the Edomites.
chapters.36.lds: Esau’s descendants have their own place in Genesis. Verse 31 says Edom had kings before Israel did. Why might Genesis keep a careful record of Esau’s family?
chapters.37.summary: Israel loves seventeen-year-old Joseph most and gives him a tunic of many colors. His brothers hate him more when he dreams that they bow to him. Jacob sends Joseph to check on his brothers near Shechem. They plan to kill him, but Reuben persuades them to throw him in a pit. Judah proposes selling him, and he is sold for twenty pieces of silver. The brothers dip his tunic in goat’s blood and show it to their father. Jacob decides an animal killed Joseph and refuses comfort. In Egypt Joseph is sold to Potiphar, Pharaoh’s captain of the guard.
chapters.37.lds: Joseph loses home through his brothers’ choices. The brothers ask Jacob to “examine” the tunic (verse 32). Who used goat skins to trick a father in chapter 27?
chapters.38.summary: Judah marries a Canaanite woman and has three sons: Er, Onan, and Shelah. Er marries Tamar and dies. Onan refuses to give his brother an heir and also dies. Judah sends Tamar home and keeps Shelah from her. Later Tamar veils herself by the road, and Judah takes her for a prostitute. He leaves his signet, cord, and staff as a pledge, and she conceives. When Judah hears she is pregnant, he orders her burned. She sends him the pledge, and he says she is more righteous than he.
chapters.38.lds: Judah admits that Tamar has a stronger claim. Judah says, “She is more righteous than I” (verse 26). What reason does he give?
chapters.39.summary: Potiphar, an Egyptian officer, buys Joseph. The LORD is with Joseph, and Potiphar puts him over his whole house. Potiphar’s wife asks Joseph to lie with her, and he refuses. He says it would wrong his master and be a sin against God. One day she grabs his garment, and he runs out and leaves it. She tells the household and her husband that the Hebrew servant came at her. Potiphar puts Joseph in the king’s prison. The LORD is with him there, and the keeper puts him over the prisoners.
chapters.39.lds: Joseph refuses sexual wrongdoing and faces a false charge. What two reasons does he give for refusing in verses 8–9?
chapters.40.summary: Pharaoh’s chief cup bearer and chief baker are jailed where Joseph is held. Joseph looks after them. Each has a dream on the same night, and Joseph sees they are sad. He says interpretations belong to God and asks to hear the dreams. He tells the cup bearer he will get his post back in three days. He asks the cup bearer to remember him and speak to Pharaoh. He tells the baker he will be hanged in three days. Both things happen on Pharaoh’s birthday, and the cup bearer forgets Joseph.
chapters.40.lds: Joseph serves others while he waits in prison. He asks the cup bearer to “remember me” (verse 14). What does verse 23 say happened?
chapters.41.summary: Two years later Pharaoh dreams of seven fat cows eaten by seven thin ones. He also dreams of seven good heads of grain swallowed by seven thin ones. No wise man can explain it, and the cup bearer remembers Joseph. Joseph says the answer is not in him but comes from God. The dreams mean seven years of plenty and then seven of famine. He advises storing a fifth of each harvest under a wise man. Pharaoh sets Joseph over all Egypt and gives him his ring and a wife. Joseph stores grain, has two sons, and sells grain when the famine comes.
chapters.41.lds: Joseph prepares for famine after explaining the dreams. He tells Pharaoh the answer is not in him (verse 16). What plan does he give in verses 33–36?
chapters.42.summary: Jacob sends ten sons to Egypt for grain but keeps Benjamin home. They bow before Joseph, the governor, and do not know him. Joseph knows them, remembers his dreams, and calls them spies. He holds them three days, then keeps Simeon and demands Benjamin. The brothers say to each other that they are guilty about Joseph. Joseph understands them and turns away to weep. He fills their sacks and puts their money back in them. Back home, Jacob refuses to let Benjamin go.
chapters.42.lds: The brothers begin to acknowledge their earlier harm. They say, “We are certainly guilty concerning our brother” (verse 21). What do they remember Joseph doing in the pit?
chapters.43.summary: The grain runs out, and Jacob tells his sons to buy more. Judah says they cannot go without Benjamin. He offers himself as a pledge for the boy’s return. Israel agrees and sends gifts and double money. In Egypt, Joseph has the brothers brought to his house, and they fear a trap. The steward calms them and brings Simeon out. Joseph sees Benjamin, leaves the room, and weeps. The brothers are seated by age, and Benjamin gets five times as much food.
chapters.43.lds: Judah accepts responsibility for Benjamin. He tells his father, “I’ll be collateral for him” (verse 9). How does that differ from his plan for Joseph in 37:26–27?
chapters.44.summary: Joseph has his silver cup hidden in Benjamin’s sack. His steward overtakes the brothers and finds it there. They tear their clothes and all return to the city. Judah says God has found out their guilt, and all will be slaves. Joseph says only the one with the cup will stay. Judah steps close and tells of their old father and his love for the boy. He says the father will die if Benjamin does not return. He asks to stay as a slave in the boy’s place.
chapters.44.lds: Judah offers his own freedom for Benjamin. He asks to stay “instead of the boy” (verse 33). Whose pain does he want to prevent in verse 34?
chapters.45.summary: Joseph can no longer hold back and sends everyone else out. He weeps aloud and says, “I am Joseph!” His brothers are too afraid to answer. He says not to be angry, because God sent him ahead to save lives. Five years of famine remain, so they must bring his father to Goshen. He weeps on Benjamin and kisses all his brothers. Pharaoh sends wagons and promises the best of Egypt. Jacob’s heart faints at the news, then revives when he sees the wagons.
chapters.45.lds: Joseph speaks truth about the sale while preserving the family. He says both “you sold me” and “God sent me” (verse 5). How can both be true?
chapters.46.summary: Israel sets out and offers sacrifices at Beersheba. God tells him in a night vision not to fear going to Egypt. God will make him a great nation there and bring him back. Jacob’s sons carry him, their wives, and their children in Pharaoh’s wagons. The chapter lists the family by mother, seventy people in all. Judah goes ahead to lead the way to Goshen. Joseph meets his father and weeps on his neck for a long time. He tells his brothers to say they are herdsmen, so they can live in Goshen.
chapters.46.lds: God reassures Jacob before the move to Egypt. God says, “I will go down with you into Egypt” (verse 4). What else does he promise in that verse?
chapters.47.summary: Joseph presents five brothers to Pharaoh, and they ask to live in Goshen as shepherds. Pharaoh gives them the best of the land. Jacob, age 130, blesses Pharaoh and calls his years few and hard. The famine grows worse. The Egyptians pay Joseph for grain with money, then with livestock. In the end they sell their land and themselves to Pharaoh. Joseph gives them seed and takes a fifth of each harvest for Pharaoh. Before he dies, Israel makes Joseph swear to bury him in Canaan.
chapters.47.lds: Joseph gives people food, but they lose land and freedom. The people say Joseph saved their lives (verse 25). What did they give up in verses 19–20?
chapters.48.summary: Joseph hears his father is sick and brings his sons Manasseh and Ephraim. Jacob recalls God’s promise at Luz and claims the two boys as his own sons. He remembers Rachel’s death on the road. Israel’s eyes are dim, and he kisses the boys. Joseph sets Manasseh, the firstborn, at Israel’s right hand. Israel crosses his hands and puts his right hand on Ephraim. Joseph objects, and his father says, “I know, my son, I know.” He sets Ephraim before Manasseh and promises that God will bring them back.
chapters.48.lds: Jacob blesses both sons and gives Ephraim the leading place. Joseph says, “Not so, my father” (verse 18). How does Jacob answer in verse 19?
chapters.49.summary: Jacob gathers his sons to tell what will come to each. Reuben, the firstborn, will not excel, because he went to his father’s bed. Simeon and Levi are cursed for their anger and will be scattered. Judah is a lion’s cub, and the ruler’s staff will stay with him. Zebulun, Issachar, Dan, Gad, Asher, and Naphtali each get a short saying. Joseph is a fruitful vine, helped by the Mighty One of Jacob. Benjamin is a hungry wolf. Jacob orders his burial in the cave at Machpelah and dies.
chapters.49.lds: Jacob’s words join blessing with consequences. He curses the anger of Simeon and Levi, not the men (verse 7). What event in chapter 34 does verse 6 recall?
chapters.50.summary: Joseph weeps over his father and has him embalmed. Egypt mourns seventy days. With Pharaoh’s leave, Joseph and a great company bury Jacob in the cave at Machpelah. Back in Egypt the brothers fear that Joseph will now repay them. They send a message asking forgiveness and bow before him. Joseph weeps and tells them not to fear. He says they meant evil, but God meant it for good, to save many lives. Dying at 110, he makes Israel swear to carry his bones out of Egypt.
chapters.50.lds: Second Nephi 3 adds Joseph’s prophecy about a future seer. The brothers fear payback after their father dies (verse 15). What question does Joseph ask in verse 19?
